spec_match.rationale: Probes navigator.gpu, adapter 'subgroups', and — the strongest part — actually compiles an `enable subgroup_uniformity;` shader and reads getCompilationInfo(); but it never consults navigator.gpu.wgslLanguageFeatures, the spec's advertised registry that the conformance suite asserts.

interactive.rationale: The check button runs the real probe chain; CDP-verified branch handling ('Supported' → 'No adapter' in this GPU-less environment).

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises checking subgroups support and testing whether a subgroup_uniformity shader compiles; that is precisely the page's flow.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles missing WebGPU, null adapter, missing subgroups feature, requestDevice failure, and compile errors — but after 'No adapter' the third row stays an unexplained '—' rather than an explicit blocked state.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5673998232977408 and the sibling pages.

conformance.rationale: Covered by the targeted feature suite (honest 3/3 env-dependent failures here); the page's compile test complements the suite's registry assertions.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Probe driven via CDP with clean console; the compile-success path needs a subgroups-capable GPU, unavailable in this environment.

telemetry_health.rationale: Server-injected /public/demo-telemetry.js verified in the served DOM.

design_system.rationale: gpu-row readouts and states use the shared variables.

accessibility.rationale: Native check button, but the three probe rows update without a live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-measured clean at 360x740 (scrollWidth 360; long code confined to scrollable pre); desktop verified via screenshot.

openQuestions.title: Add a wgslLanguageFeatures row to the probe
openQuestions.detail: navigator.gpu.wgslLanguageFeatures.has('subgroup_uniformity') is the spec's direct advertisement of this feature and needs no adapter — it would give this page a meaningful readout even on GPU-less machines and align it with the conformance suite.

openQuestions.title: Show an explicit blocked state after 'No adapter'
openQuestions.detail: When requestAdapter() returns null the subgroup_uniformity row stays '—'; set it to 'blocked — no GPU adapter' so the dead-end is explained.

summary: Honest, correctly-branched probe page whose compile-the-actual-directive test is the right idea; adding the adapter-independent wgslLanguageFeatures check would make it meaningful even where (as here) no GPU adapter exists. Verified via CDP: Supported → No adapter chain, clean console, clean layouts. Browser-verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshot + DOM dump) and raw CDP (real click dispatch, console/network capture, 360x740 DPR3 mobile emulation) — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session. Chromium 141 predates Chrome 145, so v145-only API paths were validated on their fallback branches, not the new-API success path. The single failed fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet request is environmental (blocked host) and was not counted against any page.
